text:
Leo: FYI ticket #98712 from Acme — they saw p99 jump to ~1.6s this morning for embeddings. Customer says requests should stay in us-west but traces show egress to eu-west. attaching trace id.
Cassandra: Ack, looking. Do we have request_id or org_id from the customer?
Leo: org_id=acme-inc, request_id=01H8XQ2QK3YB2Z1. They pasted a span map, see below.
Marta: :eyes: Can you drop the raw trace link? I'll check routing table and any recent peering changes.
tracebot: New trace uploaded: https://traces.redwood/01H8XQ2QK3YB2Z1 (span count 42, skewed hop: egress->eu-west-1)
Devon: Interesting — the route policy for that shard hasn't been touched in 3w. Could be client-side DNS or regional affinity flip. Any pattern in IPs?
Alex: I pulled the trace -> egress IP 3.120.45.22 which resolves to our eu-west NAT pool. We had a short NAT reassignment yesterday during capacity resharding (2024-11-17 03:12 UTC).
Cassandra: Customer is adamant they didn't change anything client-side. They repro steps: POST to /v1/embeddings with model=embed-1 and no custom region header.
Leo: They included a curl snippet:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
```
Cassandra: Also attached packet capture showing SYN->SYN-ACK path that hits our eu nat gateway.
Marta: Can we confirm if smart-routing fallback is enabled for this account? Fallback -> compatible model in eu could explain automatic reroute when us shard overloaded.
Devon: Good point. I checked account config: acme-inc has fallback enabled with cost-tier=auto and prefer_region unset. That means policy may select eu variant if us capacity busy. But p99 1.6s sounds like unexpected hop, not planned fallback.
Alex: I dug through autoscaler logs — there was a transient us-west GPU pressure spike at 03:10 UTC with several queued requests; autoscaler moved some workers but we also triggered a cross-region fallback window of ~90s for new requests.
Cassandra: So timeline matches customer repro, oof. They hit during that window. How do we avoid sending them to eu for embeddings?
Marta: Short term: disable fallback for acme-inc or pin prefer_region=us-west. Long term: we should avoid using eu model variants unless latency difference is acceptable.
Devon: I pushed a canary that prefers local shards more aggressively when client latency SLOs present. Will monitor.
Leo: Customer asked for root cause summary and repro steps to validate fix. Can we produce a one-paragraph RCA and a reproducer command they'd run after change?
Cassandra: Draft RCA: "During a brief capacity pressure event in us-west, smart-routing fallback selected an eu variant to satisfy throughput. Because acme-inc had fallback enabled and no prefer_region pinned, some requests were routed cross-region causing increased p99. A NAT reassignment made the eu egress visible in traces."
Cassandra: Repro steps for customer after we disable fallback:
```
# after we set prefer_region=us-west for org acme-inc
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -v | grep "x-redwood-region"
# expect: x-redwood-region: us-west-1
```
Marta: @Devon please add an entry to the runbook: when autoscaler spikes, ensure fallback window is limited to <30s for latency-sensitive tiers.
Devon: Adding now. Also will add a telemetry alert for cross-region egress count >0.5% of requests per minute.
Leo: I'll reply to customer with the RCA and the immediate mitigation (we set prefer_region=us-west and disabled fallback for their org) and ask them to run the repro curl.
customer_jane: Thanks team — will run the repro in 10m and report back. Appreciate the quick triage. :heart:
